content.text: {"primary_meaning":"God’s people—especially Israel, Christ’s disciples, or the church—pictured as dependent, vulnerable, and in need of divine or pastoral guidance, protection, and care from God or Christ as shepherd.","primary_basis":["Psalm 23:1-4 — the Lord is the shepherd who guides and protects his people.","Psalm 95:7 and Psalm 100:3 — God’s people are the sheep of his pasture.","Isaiah 53:6 — people are compared to sheep that have gone astray.","Ezekiel 34:1-31 — Israel is God’s flock, harmed by false shepherds and gathered by God himself.","Matthew 9:36 — the crowds are like sheep without a shepherd.","Matthew 10:6 and 15:24 — Israel is described as the lost sheep of the house of Israel.","Luke 15:3-7; Matthew 18:12-14 — the lost sheep represents a sinner or vulnerable disciple sought and restored.","John 10:1-30 — Jesus is the Good Shepherd; his sheep know his voice and follow him.","John 21:15-17 — Christ’s followers are sheep entrusted to pastoral care.","1 Peter 2:25 and 5:2-4 — believers return to the Shepherd and form the flock under pastoral oversight."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"The righteous or saved, contrasted with the wicked or condemned as goats.","basis":["Matthew 25:31-46 — the sheep at the Son of Man’s right hand inherit the kingdom, while the goats are judged."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Wayward, lost, or sinful human beings who need repentance, rescue, and restoration.","basis":["Isaiah 53:6 — all have gone astray like sheep.","Luke 15:3-7; Matthew 18:12-14 — the lost sheep is sought and restored.","1 Peter 2:25 — believers had been straying like sheep before returning to Christ."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Israel specifically, rather than God’s people in a general or ecclesial sense.","basis":["Jeremiah 50:6 — Israel is described as lost sheep.","Ezekiel 34:1-31 — the flock is explicitly Israel.","Matthew 10:6 and 15:24 — Jesus refers to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Innocent, meek, silent, or defenseless sufferers, sometimes associated especially with faithful persecution.","basis":["Isaiah 53:7 — the servant is like a sheep silent before its shearers.","Acts 8:32-35 — Isaiah’s sheep imagery is applied to Jesus.","Romans 8:36; Psalm 44:22 — God’s people are regarded as sheep for slaughter."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Sacrificial victims, with the imagery ultimately focused on Christ’s atoning death.","basis":["Isaiah 53:7 — the suffering servant is led like a sheep to slaughter.","Acts 8:32-35 — the slaughtered sheep imagery is interpreted christologically.","Although related, New Testament sacrificial symbolism more characteristically calls Christ the 'Lamb of God' in John 1:29, 36 and Revelation 5."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Believers or missionaries sent into a hostile world in a condition of vulnerability.","basis":["Matthew 10:16 — disciples are sent as sheep among wolves.","Luke 10:3 — the sent disciples are like lambs among wolves."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a broad consensus that sheep most often symbolize people under shepherding, particularly God’s covenant people or Christ’s followers. The precise emphasis varies by passage: dependence and belonging, straying and restoration, righteous status, vulnerability, or sacrificial suffering. Thus the general symbolism is settled, but no single nuance applies uniformly in every biblical context."}
